Case study summary

What did Juan build?

A centralized service and payment website for a South Florida landscaping company.

This case study was last reviewed on July 26, 2026. Project details and limitations are identified throughout the page.

Role, audience and objectives

Responsibility carried through the system.

Juan's role

  • Strategy and information architecture
  • Visual and responsive design
  • SitePad development
  • Content structure and forms
  • Business email infrastructure
  • Payment pathways and domain configuration

Audience

  • South Florida homeowners
  • Commercial property teams
  • Customers returning to make a service payment

Objectives

  • Make a broad service offering easier to scan
  • Support both inquiry and payment tasks
  • Establish visible local context

Behavioral lens

  • Orientation through clear grouping
  • Reduced uncertainty at decision points

Context

Sharper Image Services needed one place for a wide service range: landscaping, lawn maintenance, hydroseeding, watering, grading, company information, estimates, location details, and direct payment.

Juan’s role

Juan handled the complete website process independently for the client, from structure and visual direction through SitePad implementation, responsive behavior, forms, business email, payment pathways, domain configuration, and launch support.

Important decision

The website separates service discovery from payment without making either feel secondary. A new customer can learn and request an estimate; a returning customer can move directly to the relevant payment route.

Evidence and limits

The site is live and its current structure is observable. No conversion, revenue, traffic, or satisfaction claims are made because approved metrics were not supplied.

Information architecture and visual direction

Important structural decisions.

Information architecture

  • Service overview
  • Company information
  • Estimate request
  • Contact and location
  • Service-specific payments

Design decisions

  • Grouped related land and landscape services without flattening their differences
  • Kept inquiry, phone, map, and payment pathways visible
  • Used service-specific payment buttons to reduce ambiguity

Technical implementation

Infrastructure, responsive behavior, and access.

Email, forms, payments and platform

  • SitePad website
  • Business email
  • Contact form
  • Service-specific payment pathways
  • Map and location integration
  • Domain and launch configuration

Accessibility and responsive design

  • Clear service labels
  • Multiple contact options
  • Responsive reading order

Available evidence

What can—and cannot—be claimed.

Available outcomes

  • A live central hub for services, inquiries, location details, and payments

Limitations

  • No client-approved performance metrics are available
  • Photography and brand-asset authorship are not claimed

Reflection

What the project clarified.

The useful work was not simply putting services online. It was giving different customer intentions a clear place to begin.
